citation.authors: Chang CJ, O'Brien KM, Keil AP, Gaston SA et al
citation.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute

record.population: 33,947 US women aged 35-74 in the Sister Study (racially and ethnically diverse)
record.design: Prospective cohort, average 10.9 years; 378 uterine cancers
record.finding: Ever use of straightening products in the previous year was associated with higher uterine cancer rates (hazard ratio 1.80, 95% CI 1.12-2.88); more than 4 uses in the previous year, 2.55 (1.46-4.45). Dyes and perms were not associated. The authors call it the first epidemiological evidence of this link and say more research is warranted.
record.note: Mixed-race cohort; the abstract does not break the result out by race. Self-reported use in the prior 12 months.
